s1.syndrome_frame: chronic foot pain with soft-tissue nodules and nerve involvement
salient_findings: pain in the plantar aspect of the left foot
three prominent, soft-tissue nodules with swelling and tenderness
numbness in the medial distal plantar foot
key_facts: 19-year-old woman
18-month history of pain in the plantar aspect of her left foot
pain was moderate initially and worsened at night
pain was exacerbated by compression and exposure to cold
three soft-tissue nodules were palpated in the plantar aspect of the left foot
nodules were mobile and not adherent to surrounding tissue
sensation testing revealed numbness in the medial distal plantar foot
toe and foot motor strength were normal
magnetic resonance imaging showed three nodules in the mid-plantar region
lesions were homogeneously isointense to skeletal muscle on T1-weighted images
lesions were homogeneously hyperintense without cystic degeneration on T2-weighted fat-suppressed images
lesions followed the course of branches of the common plantar digital nerves

shortlist.label: plexiform schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: multiple soft-tissue nodules with nerve involvement and characteristic 'mouse-tail' sign on MRI

shortlist.label: glomus tumor
shortlist.why_kept: pain exacerbated by compression and exposure to cold, and lesions following the course of branches of the common plantar digital nerves

shortlist.label: neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: multiple soft-tissue nodules with nerve involvement and absence of family history of neurofibromatosis

shortlist.label: schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: lesions following the course of branches of the common plantar digital nerves and homogeneous signal on MRI

shortlist.label: neurilemmoma
shortlist.why_kept: nerve sheath origin and homogeneous signal on MRI, although less specific than plexiform schwannoma

raw.rationale: The clinical presentation of multiple soft-tissue nodules in the plantar aspect of the foot, along with the imaging findings of multiple nodules following the course of branches of the common plantar digital nerves, is most consistent with plexiform schwannoma. The lesions' homogeneous isointensity to skeletal muscle on T1-weighted images and homogeneous hyperintensity on T2-weighted fat-suppressed images also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: glomus tumor
rejected.why: Glomus tumors are typically smaller, more painful, and have a stronger association with cold exposure, but the presence of multiple nodules and their specific imaging characteristics make plexiform schwannoma a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: neurofibroma
rejected.why: Neurofibromas can present as multiple soft-tissue nodules, but the specific imaging characteristics and the lack of a reported family history of neurofibromatosis make plexiform schwannoma more likely.

rejected.label: schwannoma
rejected.why: While schwannoma is a possible diagnosis, the presence of multiple nodules arranged in a linear distribution, as seen in this case, is more characteristic of plexiform schwannoma.

rejected.label: neurilemmoma
rejected.why: Neurilemmoma is another term for schwannoma, but the specific characteristics of this case, including the multiple nodules and their imaging appearance, make plexiform schwannoma the more specific and likely diagnosis.
